title: The Big Freeze
liner_notes: 1996: Arctic September sea ice hit an all-time record high of 7.58 M km², 1.3 σ above the 1983–2012 average.

title: Fire Regime Shift
liner_notes: 2002: U.S. wildfire area burned shifted to a new normal — its 5-year average rose from 4.16 M acres to 7.56 M acres.

title: Fire Climbs Higher
liner_notes: 2004: U.S. wildfire area burned set a new record high of 8.10 M acres (1.2 σ above the 1983–2012 average), a record that stood until 2005. NIFC's 2004 figure excludes North Carolina state lands.

title: Firestorm
liner_notes: 2005: U.S. wildfire area burned set a new record high of 8.69 M acres (1.4 σ above the 1983–2012 average), a record that stood until 2006.

title: Record Burn
liner_notes: 2006: U.S. wildfire area burned set a new record high of 9.87 M acres (1.9 σ above the 1983–2012 average), a record that stood until 2015.

title: Record Melt
liner_notes: 2007: Arctic September sea ice set a new record low of 4.27 M km² (1.9 σ below the 1983–2012 average), a record that stood until 2012.

title: The Ice Retreat
liner_notes: 2007: Arctic September sea ice shifted to a new normal — its 5-year average fell from 5.86 M km² to 4.73 M km².

title: The Great Melt
liner_notes: 2012: Arctic September sea ice hit an all-time record low of 3.57 M km², 2.5 σ below the 1983–2012 average.

title: Ice Rebound
liner_notes: 2013: the biggest one-year rise in the record — Arctic September sea ice rose by 1.64 M km² from 2012, to 5.21 M km².

title: The Big Lull
liner_notes: 2013: the biggest one-year drop in the record — U.S. wildfire area burned fell by 5.01 M acres from 2012, to 4.32 M acres.

title: Turning Up the Heat
liner_notes: 2015: the global temperature anomaly set a new record high of +0.89 °C (2.5 σ above the 1983–2012 average), a record that stood until 2016.

title: The Warming Shift
liner_notes: 2015: the global temperature anomaly shifted to a new normal — its 5-year average rose from +0.68 °C to +0.93 °C.

title: Year of Fire
liner_notes: 2015: U.S. wildfire area burned hit an all-time record high of 10.12 M acres, 2.0 σ above the 1983–2012 average.

title: Fever Pitch
liner_notes: 2016: the global temperature anomaly set a new record high of +1.01 °C (3.2 σ above the 1983–2012 average), a record that stood until 2023.

title: Warm Spell
liner_notes: 2019: the global temperature anomaly reached +0.98 °C, 3.0 σ above the 1983–2012 average.

title: Heatwave Year
liner_notes: 2020: the global temperature anomaly reached +1.01 °C, 3.2 σ above the 1983–2012 average.

title: Thin Ice
liner_notes: 2020: Arctic September sea ice reached 4.00 M km², 2.1 σ below the 1983–2012 average.

title: New Heat Record
liner_notes: 2023: the global temperature anomaly set a new record high of +1.17 °C (4.1 σ above the 1983–2012 average), a record that stood until 2024.

title: Hottest Year on Record
liner_notes: 2024: the global temperature anomaly hit an all-time record high of +1.28 °C, 4.7 σ above the 1983–2012 average.

title: Running Hot
liner_notes: 2025: the global temperature anomaly reached +1.18 °C, 4.1 σ above the 1983–2012 average.
